claims.title: Authorization-code prefix matching can disclose a member authorization code to an attacker-controlled redirect
claims.description: An attacker can register or use a redirect URI beginning with a partner's registered prefix and cause `process:authorization-server` to return a member's authorization code over `flow:entity:member>entity:partner-app>return-with-authorization-code` to that attacker-controlled endpoint. This is a disclosure of a credential, not wire interception: HTTPS protects the transport but the authorization server itself hands the code to the selected redirect. The code can be exchanged through `flow:entity:partner-app>process:authorization-server>token-requests` for bearer access tokens; because every partner receives every scope, the resulting token can reach `process:rewards-api` for member balances and gift-card redemptions.

quotes.text: the authorization server accepts any redirect URI that starts with it.
The team gives every partner app every scope

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because exploiting a prefix-matched redirect requires a crafted URI associated with a registered partner, but the authorization server explicitly accepts such prefixes. Impact is high because the disclosed authorization code can yield bearer access tokens with every partner scope, which reach `process:rewards-api` data and redemption operations.

mitigations.summary: Require exact redirect-URI matching
mitigations.detail: Store and compare complete normalized redirect URIs, rejecting prefix, wildcard, and partial matches before issuing an authorization response.

mitigations.summary: Bind authorization codes to the legitimate client
mitigations.detail: Require PKCE for the public mobile client and bind each authorization code to its client and redirect URI so a delivered code cannot be redeemed by another party.

claims.title: A stolen mobile refresh token remains a long-lived source of bearer access
claims.description: `process:mobile-app` keeps a credential-bearing refresh token on a member-controlled phone. An attacker who extracts that token from a stolen or compromised device can use `flow:process:mobile-app>process:authorization-server>token-requests` to obtain new access tokens repeatedly. The token's sliding lifetime means the attacker can preserve access by using it; the resulting bearer tokens reach `process:rewards-api` for balances, points transactions, and gift-card redemptions.

quotes.text: The app keeps a refresh token on the phone. A mobile refresh token never expires: every time the app uses it, its expiry slides forward another ninety days.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because the attacker must obtain access to a member device or its application data, but the refresh token is deliberately retained on that device and remains renewable. Impact is high because a recovered bearer refresh token produces access tokens that reach `process:rewards-api` functions involving `pii` and financial rewards.

mitigations.summary: Protect and bound mobile refresh tokens
mitigations.detail: Store refresh tokens only in platform-backed hardware or secure storage, rotate them on use, enforce absolute and idle expirations, and revoke the token family when reuse is detected.

mitigations.summary: Use sender-constrained tokens where feasible
mitigations.detail: Bind refresh-token use to an app-held key or device attestation so an extracted token alone cannot be replayed from another device.

claims.title: Unverified transport to the identity database may expose password hashes and refresh tokens
claims.description: `flow:process:authorization-server>store:identity-database>read-and-write-accounts-and-grants` has `encryption_in_transit: unknown`. If this internal database segment is not encrypted, an attacker able to observe the cloud path can intercept member accounts, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents sent between `process:authorization-server` and `store:identity-database`. Recovered refresh tokens or codes can then be used against `process:authorization-server` to obtain bearer access; this draft is conditional on the unresolved transport-protection attribute, not an assertion that the connection is plaintext.

quotes.text: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database, together with the authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents it issues.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the transport protection is unverified and the attacker must obtain an on-path position within `boundary:rewards-cloud`. Impact is high because the flow carries password hashes and reusable authorization credentials for the identity system.

mitigations.summary: Verify and require encrypted database transport
mitigations.detail: Set `encryption_in_transit` for `flow:process:authorization-server>store:identity-database>read-and-write-accounts-and-grants` to TLS with certificate validation, preferably mTLS for the database client and server.

mitigations.summary: Minimize credentials in ordinary database exchanges
mitigations.detail: Use short-lived, rotated authorization artifacts and ensure application telemetry does not duplicate credential-bearing database payloads.

claims.title: Unverified rewards-API-to-ledger transport may expose member balances and transactions
claims.description: `flow:process:rewards-api>store:points-ledger>read-and-write-points` has `encryption_in_transit: unknown`. If transport encryption is absent or terminates before this segment, an on-path attacker can intercept balance reads and points transactions between `process:rewards-api` and `store:points-ledger`. The captured financial activity can be correlated with requests handled by the public API and used to target members; this is conditional on the currently unverified encryption state.

quotes.text: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction.
Nobody recorded how the rewards API connects to the ledger

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the internal transport control is unknown and observation requires a cloud-network foothold. Impact is high because the ledger contains every member's financial balances and transaction history.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the rewards API ledger connection
mitigations.detail: Require TLS with validated service and database identities for `flow:process:rewards-api>store:points-ledger>read-and-write-points`, including any internal hop.

claims.title: Unverified transport to the API log store may expose captured bearer tokens
claims.description: `flow:process:rewards-api>store:api-log-store>write-request-log` has `encryption_in_transit: unknown` and sends request headers containing bearer access tokens. If this link lacks verified encryption, an on-path attacker can intercept those tokens while `process:rewards-api` writes them to `store:api-log-store`. The attacker can then present a captured token to `process:rewards-api` and read or act on the associated member's rewards account; this draft is conditional on the unknown transport setting.

quotes.text: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the log-transport encryption is unverified and an attacker needs an on-path cloud position. Impact is high because the payload contains bearer access tokens that can be replayed to the internet-facing `process:rewards-api`.

mitigations.summary: Use authenticated TLS for log delivery
mitigations.detail: Require TLS with endpoint authentication for `flow:process:rewards-api>store:api-log-store>write-request-log` rather than relying on an internal network segment.

mitigations.summary: Stop transmitting bearer tokens to logs
mitigations.detail: Redact Authorization headers at `process:rewards-api` before log events are created, so log delivery cannot carry replayable credentials.

claims.title: Unverified support-console database transport may disclose account-closure data
claims.description: `flow:process:support-console>store:identity-database>close-accounts` has `encryption_in_transit: unknown`. If the connection is not protected end-to-end, an attacker on the internal path can intercept account-closure records and associated member identifiers as `process:support-console` writes to `store:identity-database`. Those identifiers reveal account status and can be correlated with the identity records held by the same store; this is conditional on the unresolved transport control.

quotes.text: Nobody recorded how the support console connects to the identity database

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because encryption for the internal connection is unverified and the attacker needs an on-path foothold. Impact is medium because the flow concerns member account closures and reaches the identity database containing member identity data.

mitigations.summary: Require TLS for support-console database access
mitigations.detail: Configure mutually authenticated TLS and certificate validation on `flow:process:support-console>store:identity-database>close-accounts` and verify the protection applies to every internal segment.

claims.title: An identity-database snapshot may disclose passwords and refresh tokens if at-rest encryption is absent
claims.description: `store:identity-database` has `encryption_at_rest: unknown`. If that unknown resolves to unencrypted storage, an attacker who obtains a database volume, backup, snapshot, or decommissioned media can read member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents without using the authorization server's normal access path. Refresh tokens and authorization artifacts can then be used to reach `process:authorization-server`; this is explicitly a conditional storage-copy threat rather than a claim that encryption is absent.

quotes.text: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database, together with the authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents it issues.
Nobody recorded how any of the three stores is protected at rest.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the at-rest control is unverified and the attacker must obtain an operational copy. Impact is high because one copy exposes member PII, password hashes, and reusable authorization credentials for the identity system.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the identity database and all operational copies
mitigations.detail: Use managed-key or customer-managed-key encryption for `store:identity-database`, backups, snapshots, replicas, and decommissioned media, while restricting export and decrypt permissions.

mitigations.summary: Limit the value of copied credentials
mitigations.detail: Hash passwords with a modern adaptive password hash and use short-lived, rotating authorization credentials with revocation on suspected copy exposure.

claims.title: A points-ledger copy may disclose the full member rewards history if encryption at rest is absent
claims.description: `store:points-ledger` has `encryption_at_rest: unknown`. If storage encryption is not present, an attacker holding a copied volume, backup, or snapshot can read every member balance and points transaction directly, bypassing `process:rewards-api`. The corpus can expose members' financial rewards activity and can be correlated with data obtained through other API interactions; this draft is conditional on the unresolved at-rest protection.

quotes.text: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction.
Nobody recorded how any of the three stores is protected at rest.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because obtaining a storage copy is required and encryption is unverified. Impact is high because one ledger copy exposes every member's balance and complete points-transaction history.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt ledger storage and copies
mitigations.detail: Require encryption at rest with managed keys for `store:points-ledger`, including snapshots, exports, replicas, and backups, and tightly restrict storage-layer access.

claims.title: An API-log-store copy may disclose replayable bearer tokens if encryption at rest is absent
claims.description: `store:api-log-store` has `encryption_at_rest: unknown` and contains request headers including bearer access tokens. If the store or its backups are unencrypted, an attacker with a copied volume or snapshot can read tokens without authenticating to `process:rewards-api`. A still-valid token can then be replayed to the public rewards API to access balances, transactions, and gift-card redemption functions; this is conditional on the unknown encryption state.

quotes.text: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.
Access tokens are signed JWTs that live for one hour, and they are plain bearer tokens.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the attacker must obtain a log-store copy and encryption at rest is unverified. Impact is high because copied logs contain plain bearer tokens that can be replayed to the internet-facing `process:rewards-api`.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt log-store media and operational copies
mitigations.detail: Apply managed-key encryption and restrictive export, backup, and snapshot permissions to `store:api-log-store`.

mitigations.summary: Remove bearer tokens from stored logs
mitigations.detail: Redact Authorization headers before records are written, then rotate any tokens that may already have been logged.

claims.title: Logging Authorization headers discloses bearer tokens to log readers
claims.description: `process:rewards-api` writes every incoming request, including headers, to `store:api-log-store`, thereby materializing bearer access tokens in a logging system. An authorized log reader acting beyond its operational purpose, or anyone who gains that reader's access, can recover a token and replay it to `process:rewards-api` during its validity period. This is distinct from a storage-copy exposure: the failed control is token capture at the logging call site, and encryption at rest would not stop a legitimate log reader from seeing the token.

quotes.text: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.
Access tokens are signed JWTs that live for one hour, and they are plain bearer tokens.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because the attacker needs log-reading access or a compromised log-reader account, while the model leaves authentication on the log-write path unverified. Impact is high because the captured credential is a plain bearer token that reaches `process:rewards-api` and its member financial functions.

mitigations.summary: Redact credentials before logging
mitigations.detail: Configure `process:rewards-api` to remove Authorization headers and other secrets before creating records for `store:api-log-store`.

mitigations.summary: Constrain log access and rotate exposed tokens
mitigations.detail: Use separate least-privilege log-reader principals, audit token-like reads, and revoke or rotate tokens that may have been recorded.

claims.title: Compromise of the authorization server may disclose the entire identity database through its reader access
claims.description: `process:authorization-server` reads and writes `store:identity-database` through `flow:process:authorization-server>store:identity-database>read-and-write-accounts-and-grants`. An attacker running code in the internet-facing authorization server can use that established reader path to retrieve member accounts, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents. This does not depend on at-rest encryption: the database returns records to its application reader. Authentication on the database flow is unknown, so the scope and isolation of that reader grant need verification; recovered refresh tokens also enable follow-on access through the authorization server.

quotes.text: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database, together with the authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents it issues.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because code execution in the internet-facing `process:authorization-server` is a prerequisite, and the authentication and scope of its database path are unverified. Impact is high because that reader path reaches password hashes, PII, authorization codes, and refresh tokens for the identity population.

mitigations.summary: Constrain the authorization server's database grant
mitigations.detail: Use a dedicated, least-privilege database identity with separate read and write permissions, limited columns, and monitored bulk-read behavior.

mitigations.summary: Isolate and harden the authorization server
mitigations.detail: Run the public authorization service with minimal host privileges, restrict database network access to its workload identity, and detect anomalous identity-record extraction.

claims.title: Compromise of the rewards API may disclose the full points ledger through its existing reader access
claims.description: `process:rewards-api` reads `store:points-ledger` through `flow:process:rewards-api>store:points-ledger>read-and-write-points`. An attacker who runs code in the internet-facing API can invoke that reader path to extract member balances and every points transaction. At-rest encryption would not prevent this because the application is an authorized store reader; the authentication on its ledger connection is unknown, so the grant's scope and isolation remain an unresolved condition. The extracted corpus can be correlated with the API's member-facing activity to profile members and target valuable balances.

quotes.text: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because the attacker must first execute code in the internet-facing `process:rewards-api`, and the ledger authentication scope is unknown. Impact is high because the authorized reader reaches every member's balance and complete transaction history.

mitigations.summary: Minimize the rewards API ledger grant
mitigations.detail: Give `process:rewards-api` narrowly scoped database permissions, split read roles from transaction-writing roles, and enforce row and column limits where feasible.

mitigations.summary: Detect corpus-scale reads
mitigations.detail: Audit and alert on ledger reads by the rewards API identity that exceed normal per-member request patterns.
